title: The Oath of the Weeping Wood Revisited
premise: Ulyana Zhou fled her hedge-witch mistress years ago, hiding among smugglers in the Thornfell mountains, until prayers start being answered by old gods who have been silent for a century—and one of them answers hers. The gods are waking because the covenant that binds the mortal realm to theirs is unraveling, and the weeping wood at Thornfell's heart, where the oath was first sworn, is dying tree by tree. Hunted by a crown inquisitor who believes the gods' return means conquest, and guided by a found family of smugglers, a defrocked priest, and a god who remembers being human, Ulyana must reforge the covenant with their own blood and memory as the binding ink. In the end, Ulyana chooses to stay visible—claiming the apprenticeship they once ran from—and the covenant is remade not on obedience, as the old oath demanded, but on freely given remembrance, at the cost of the god who loved them forgetting their name.
about_author: Mara Amberdale is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade drawing mountain passes before trading maps for myths. They write fantasy about people who inherit burdens they never asked to carry.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Psalter
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Running contraband through the Thornfell passes, Ulyana prays out of habit to a god everyone says is dead—and the prayer is answered with a falling star and a voice in the weeping wood. Emotional beat: the terror of being seen for the first time in years.

chapters.title: What the Hedge-Witch Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with letters from the past. Ulyana returns, against every instinct, to the burned-out cottage of the mistress they abandoned, finding her grimoire and a covenant fragment naming Ulyana's bloodline as oath-keepers. Beat: grief braided with guilt.

chapters.title: The Company of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Multiple POV, anchored on smuggler captain Brek Onda. Brek's crew debates sheltering Ulyana, a walking heresy with a price on their head; the defrocked priest Sef joins, recognizing the covenant fragment. Beat: found family forming around a dangerous secret.

chapters.title: A God Who Remembers Being Human
chapters.summary: The god Veyl's POV. Veyl, waking weak in the weeping wood, recalls the century of silence and the human he was before the oath took his name. He tests Ulyana's worthiness and finds them wanting—and honest about it. Beat: wary tenderness between mortal and divine.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Halvard's POV. Halvard traces answered prayers like a blood trail, burning a village shrine and interrogating Sef's sister. He is not a zealot but a grieving man who blames the gods for his daughter's death. Beat: the antagonist made sympathetic and frightening.

chapters.title: Roots Under the Snow
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The company treks to the heart of the weeping wood, where trees die as the covenant frays, and Ulyana learns the original oath was sworn on a child's memory—deliberately, by their ancestor. Beat: horror at one's inheritance, and the choice to keep walking anyway.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Pass of Knives
chapters.summary: Brek's POV. A crew member sells their route to Halvard; the ambush in the pass kills two smugglers and shatters the group's trust. Ulyana saves Brek with magic they swore off, revealing their power. Beat: betrayal, loss, and the cost of being visible.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Veyl's alternating POV. To reforge the covenant, someone must surrender a true memory as binding ink—and Veyl volunteers his memory of his human life, which means forgetting Ulyana. Ulyana argues, rages, and begins the rite. Beat: love measured against sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Weeping Wood Remembers
chapters.summary: Climax, all POVs converging. Halvard storms the wood mid-rite; Sef dies holding the inquisitor's blade, and his death—not vengeance—cracks Halvard open. Ulyana speaks the new covenant aloud: remembrance freely given, not obedience compelled. Beat: climax through witness, not battle.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. The wood greens again; Veyl, nameless and human-hearted, tends it without knowing why Ulyana visits every week. Ulyana takes up the hedge-witch's cottage and apprentices, openly, to the mountain itself. Beat: bittersweet resolution—inheritance accepted, memory carried for two.
